scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths - success and failure - and a caller can tell which without parsing prose

evidence.asserts: The layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths, success and failure, and a caller can tell which without parsing prose. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source: http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts that error bodies carry all four envelope keys and that the HTTP status agrees with the body. A structural check - does the function import _shared/envelope.ts - would be the wrong prover here and R6 would refuse it, because importing the module is not the same as returning the envelope when the path fails.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - the envelope and the status agree with the body on all 40 relations probed. The gate also measures the harder half and reports it rather than hiding it: 27 of those relations CANNOT distinguish refusal from absence, which is PostgREST + RLS by construction rather than a defect patchable at the relation. What makes that acceptable is that every page reading them answers the question at its own layer, and the gate counts how: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1. A prover returning a bare PASS over 40 relations while 27 were structurally ambiguous would assert more than it measured. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the gate, so a change to the functions or migrations under this claim still expires it; replay re-earns it in one command.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying data. Disagreement is measured on the wire, not inferred

evidence.asserts: The HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying a success. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source - http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts the status matches what the body actually says. This is the behavioural half of the envelope contract and cannot be settled structurally: a function can import the envelope helper and still answer 200 with an error inside, which is precisely the shape that makes a failed read look like an empty one to every caller downstream.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - status and body agree on all 40 relations probed, across anon, member and no-key callers. The gate reports what it cannot settle instead of smoothing it: 27 relations cannot distinguish refusal from absence, PostgREST + RLS by construction, each answered at the page layer rather than the relation (redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1). That distinction matters more for THIS oracle than most, because a 200 carrying zero rows is exactly how a refusal disguises itself as an absence - the same class this platform hit when a failed read rendered as 'no contacts saved yet', and when a zero-row update returned no error and a reporter was told their report had been sent. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration beneath the claim still expires it - as it did within this same session, when migration ...000068 landed after these rows were first banked and correctly staled the ones resting on migrations.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the same call twice produces ONE effect; the second is refused or absorbed, and the count in the DB proves which

evidence.asserts: The same ordered read, issued twice over two SEPARATE connections, returns the same bytes: a repeat read is not quietly a different read. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - read_idempotency re-issues every repeatable read on the platform and compares a digest that is itself proven sensitive, so a match means agreement rather than a digest too coarse to notice a difference.
evidence.checked: Run live this session across all 22 pages: 93 repeatable reads, PASS - every repeatable read returned identical bytes across two separate connections. The sub-verdicts are carried here rather than flattened into the headline: 83 plain idempotent, 5 idempotent-uncontrolled (repeatable, but with no control proving the digest would have caught a change), 2 idempotent-modulo-clock, 2 CONTROL-FAILED and 1 UNKNOWN. Those last three are not passes and are recorded as such - a row claiming clean green while 3 reads never produced a verdict would be the vacuous match this gate exists to refuse.

evidence.restamped_at: 2026-08-22 — gate read_idempotency re-ran green against the current state (read_idempotency_report.json); sha re-anchored, claim unchanged

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: a paginated or sorted read has a TOTAL order - re-running it does not reshuffle equal keys, so page 2 cannot repeat or skip a row from page 1

evidence.asserts: A paginated or sorted read at this layer has a TOTAL order: re-running it returns the same rows in the same sequence, so no row appears on two pages and none is skipped. Proven by a REGISTERED gate rather than a session - paginated-order-totality scans every paged-and-ordered query chain on the platform and fails if one ends without a unique tiebreaker, holding forward-only at 0. R2 turns this row INVALID rather than silently green if that gate is deleted or renamed.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: 176 paginated+ordered chains scanned platform-wide, 0 non-total, ratchet PASS at 0, and the gate's selftest passes BOTH directions - it catches a non-total order and accepts a tiebreakered one, which separates a working scanner from one that approves everything. The run also caught a regression introduced earlier in this same session (report-sender.html loadBounces ordering on triggered_at with no tiebreaker, 0 -> 1), fixed to .order('id') and back to 0. depends_on names the SUBJECT artifacts as well as the gate: anchoring to the gate alone was refused by R7, correctly - a page or migration that changes the query must expire the claim about it. Gate-backing buys a one-command recovery via replay, not immunity from staleness.
evidence.value_checked: gate:paginated-order-totality | 176 chains scanned, 0 non-total, forward-only PASS | selftest both directions | caught+fixed this session: report-sender.html:1357 order(triggered_at) | depends_on: achievements.html, tools/validate_paginated_order_totality.py, utils.js
evidence.restamped_at: 2026-08-22 — gate paginated-order-totality re-ran green against the current state (paginated_order_totality_report.json); sha re-anchored, claim unchanged

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the value carries its unit at the boundary (pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent) - the class that made a knob of 10 mean 1000%

evidence.asserts: A value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY - pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent - so no consumer has to infer the scale. This is the class the oracle names as having made a knob of 10 mean 1000%. Proven by a registered gate: units_at_boundary requires every money, credit, percent and duration column to declare its unit by CHECK, comment, sibling unit column or name, and fails outright if any column mixes two scales.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS WITH DEBT, and the debt is recorded rather than rounded off. MIXED-SCALE = 0, the hard invariant that produces the 10-means-1000% failure. Two columns carry their unit only by convention and are reported, not failed: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent) and service_credit_ledger.amount (money), each with no CHECK, no comment, no sibling unit column and a name that does not say; five more are undecl-latent. Those seven are real debt against this oracle and are named so they can be closed rather than rediscovered. The gate was matched to the oracle deliberately: the oracle says the value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY and names the mixed-scale failure, which is this gate's subject - the neighbouring prove_units_visible answers a different question (what a reader sees) and would have been the wrong prover.
evidence.value_checked: gate:units_at_boundary | MIXED-SCALE 0 (the hard invariant) | UNDECLARED 2: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent), service_credit_ledger.amount (money) | undecl-latent 5 | PASS with debt | depends_on: achievements.html, tools/prove_units_at_boundary.py, utils.js

evidence.asserts: What one side of the seam WRITES is what the other side READS: a value is not silently rewritten on the way in by something nobody named. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - values_survive_write extracts every trigger that assigns to NEW, classifies the rewrite by its STRUCTURE, and fails on any that belongs to no named class. It also measures the one class that can lose a person's work: every left(NEW.col, N) cap is read against the stored data, because a possible truncation and an actual one are different facts.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - every rewrite on the way in belongs to a named class, and none of the 106 capped columns has ever truncated a stored value (widest: engineering_calcs.sow_text at 984 of 4000). It earned that by first FAILING on a trigger I had added earlier in this same session: tg_community_posts_moderation_fields, which restores flagged/pinned for a caller who is not a supervisor of that hive (migrations ...000063/64, after a reported author was found clearing their own flag). The gate was right to stop it - it assigns NEW.x := OLD.x, a shape none of its four classes covered. The fix was to teach the CLASSIFIER a new structural class, field-authorization-guard, not to rename my trigger guard_* to slip past a prefix check: the function's own docstring says widening the name allowlist until the gate goes green is bending the gate, and structure is what a rewrite DOES. The new class is detected on shape - every assignment restoring the column to its own prior value - so no outside value replaces the caller's and their other edits still land.

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_null_semantics.py - 286 client coalesce sites read out of the pages and joined against the SCHEMA, so each one is judged against whether its column can actually be NULL. ★THE ORACLE'S OWN EXAMPLE IS NUMERIC: 'NULL meant no cap in the DB and arrived as a cap of ZERO in the client'. So the sites are separated by what the substitution DESTROYS, not by how many there are: numeric-substitute (50) and boolean-substitute (3) turn an UNKNOWN into a definite value and are the real class; not-null-in-db (15) cannot fire because the column is NOT NULL; visible-placeholder (47) renders an em-dash or equivalent and is the CORRECT behaviour, not a defect; text-blank (171) collapses NULL to '' where both already render as nothing - a weaker concern, recorded but not charged as this oracle's failure. ★THE DETECTOR IS PROVEN ABLE TO SEE A REAL NULL, which is what stops a clean page from being a vacuous pass: the control column v_achievement_xp_log.source_id holds 77 live NULLs and is found. A detector that cannot see that cannot see any. ★AND THE LIVE COUNT IS SEPARATE FROM THE LATENT ONE: zero of these sites is misbehaving TODAY, because the columns concerned currently hold no NULLs (0/4, 0/95, 0/97 on the ones sampled). That is a fact about this dataset, not about the code - which is precisely why the structural reading is the one banked here, and why 'no NULL has appeared yet' is not recorded as safety. FOR THIS PAGE: 12 site(s) substitute a definite value for a possibly-NULL column, which is the exact shape this oracle names. Example: `ach.current_level || 0` - column `current_level` (integer), nullable on v_worker_achievements_truth, so an UNKNOWN would arrive as 0. Not misbehaving today only because those columns currently hold no NULLs, which is a property of the data and not of the code.

findings.title: NOT BANKED - fail_401: an expired session is not surfaced honestly on this page. THIS FAILS ON 17 OF 17 PAGES WALKED, and the fix is ADOPTION, not a new message
findings.detail: FAILURE STATES ARE INJECTED, never waited for. failures() intercepts the page's own reads and answers them with the failure under test, then reads what the page TELLS A PERSON. Every mutating verb is answered by a stub rather than forwarded - decided by blockWrite across the WHOLE Supabase surface, rpc and edge functions included - so nothing reaches the shared test database. The path is verified unchanged across the injection, and the surface is asserted before it: an expired session earlier today made 19 of 22 pages return identical landing-page readings, and 3 pages were REFUSED by that guard on this very sweep rather than measured. The navigation fence held on 16 of 16 pages read. THE ORACLE IS WHAT THE READER IS TOLD, not whether an error was caught. A caught error that renders nothing is indistinguishable, from the reader's side, from success. Stamped ::v=3: the top-level digest is a SET of per-statement content hashes, so a shared-library append expires nothing while a modify or delete correctly expires. Self-tested 8/8. FINDING: Injecting a 401 into this page's reads, the page does not tell the reader their session expired, does not name the session as the cause, and does not state the consequence for what they were doing. THE REFLEX IS TO WRITE THE MISSING MESSAGE AND THAT WOULD BE WRONG - it already exists. utils.js:1568 reads 'Your session expired, so nothing was saved. Sign in again and redo this step.' and :1611 has the read equivalent, with _WH_PG_DENIAL at :1518 and a careful 401-versus-403 note beneath it. There is even a comment recording that this was fixed once on the inquiry path, where a 42501 told a SIGNED-IN buyer their session had expired, and that 'the shared helper kept the bug for every other path'. Writing a new string would add a second source of truth for text that is already correct. SO THE DEFECT IS ADOPTION: the read path catches the status and never renders whReadError's text. A uniform 17-of-17 failure is not seventeen independent lapses, it is one shared path swallowing the status - which means ONE fix earns all seventeen rows in a single sweep. Same shape as the other platform-wide finds in this arc: ::placeholder absent everywhere, companion-launcher.js with no prefers-reduced-motion block at all. AND THE PROBE IS NOT AT FAULT, which matters before acting on a 17/17 result: fail_null_field passes on 16 of 16 pages under the same injection harness. A broken probe does not pass one injection everywhere and fail another everywhere. Row stays owed; measure adoption at the point of RENDER, not by the helper's existence.

findings.title: FAILS, MEASURED, AND IT EXPLAINS A DEFECT THIS BANK ALREADY RECORDED WITHOUT A CAUSE. THE INVARIANT: a worker's stored xp_total for an achievement must equal the sum of that achievement's own award rows - the ledger IS the source, and a stored aggregate that disagrees with it is a number nobody can
findings.detail: FAILS, MEASURED, AND IT EXPLAINS A DEFECT THIS BANK ALREADY RECORDED WITHOUT A CAUSE. THE INVARIANT: a worker's stored xp_total for an achievement must equal the sum of that achievement's own award rows - the ledger IS the source, and a stored aggregate that disagrees with it is a number nobody can audit. Measured by joining worker_achievements to achievement_xp_log on (worker_name, achievement_id) and comparing the stored xp_total against sum(xp_earned). RESULT: **42 of 50 pairs disagree, worst gap 349,711 XP.** Not a rounding artefact and not a race - a gap of that size means the stored total is not derived from the log at all. WHY THIS IS THE SAME BUG AS THE NEGATIVE COUNTDOWN ALREADY ON THIS PAGE: the achievements surface was recorded earlier showing xp_into_current_level = 342,986 against xp_per_level = 100, producing xp_to_next_level = -342,886 with is_maxed false on 63 of 65 rows. That 342,986 and this 349,711 are the same order of magnitude and the same shape. The downstream arithmetic was self-consistent, which localised the fault to the INPUT - and this measurement names the input: xp_total is inflated relative to the ledger that is supposed to define it, so every column derived from it (level, progress into level, countdown to next) inherits the inflation and the countdown goes negative. One cause, two symptoms, and the symptom was found first. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A COSMETIC NUMBER: XP drives level, level drives badge tiers, and badge tiers are displayed as competence claims on a person's profile and carried into the marketplace's provider tier. An unauditable XP total is a trust claim with no ledger behind it - and this platform's own rule is that a stored aggregate must be reproducible from its log. TO FINISH (not attempted here - it is a migration, and mid-walk edits are what A15 forbids): decide which side is authoritative. If the log is (it should be - it has per-award provenance: source_action, source_id, earned_at), then recompute xp_total from it and add a constraint or a scheduled reconciliation so the two cannot drift again. If some awards were made WITHOUT a log row, those are the real gap and they need back-filling before any recompute, or workers lose XP they were legitimately given. **Check which before recomputing** - a recompute that silently deletes unlogged awards would be a second bug wearing the fix's clothes.

findings.title: The XP ledger is broken in BOTH directions - 32 log rows have no achievement row at all
findings.detail: Extends the xp_is_ledger_sum diagnosis on this page with the reverse direction, which changes what a fix must do. Already recorded: 42 of 50 (worker, achievement) pairs have a stored xp_total that disagrees with sum(xp_earned), worst gap 349,711. NOW ALSO MEASURED: **32 achievement_xp_log rows point at a (worker_name, achievement_id) pair with NO worker_achievements row at all.** So awards exist in the ledger that were never rolled up, AND stored totals exist that the ledger cannot account for. The two facts together rule out the simplest explanations: this is not a stale aggregate (that would fail in one direction) and not a missing trigger on award (that would leave totals at zero). WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE FIX SPECIFICALLY: a straight 'recompute xp_total from the log' would DESTROY the portion of the stored totals that has no log backing, and a straight 'insert missing worker_achievements rows from the log' would credit XP twice for anyone whose total is already inflated. Neither direction is safe alone. Reconcile per (worker, achievement) with the 32 orphan log rows and the 42 disagreeing pairs listed explicitly, decide per case which side is authoritative, and only then recompute - the log has per-award provenance (source_action, source_id, earned_at) to adjudicate with.

evidence.checked: PASSES, proven as a DECLARED invariant against live data: 'awarding achievement XP moves the total and the log together' returns ZERO offending rows. WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT COMPARISON FOR THIS ORACLE: achievements' ledger-conservation oracle, asked in the only way this dataset allows: the stored totals are seeded at synthetic scale and cannot be reconciled backwards, so what is proven is that a real award writes BOTH sides by the same amount. A total that moved without a log row is the one-sided write; a log row without the total is its mirror. MEASURED BY ATTEMPTING THE TRANSITION as an authenticated member in a rolled-back transaction, which is the only way a terminal state can be proven - and as the ROLE that matters: the same attempt as the postgres superuser SUCCEEDS, because the guard deliberately exempts the admin path, so a superuser probe reports the EXEMPTED path as the defect. Verdict: BEGIN CREATE TABLE DO PAIRED total +7 and exactly 1 log row ROLLBACK. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT: any offending row at all - the check reports the offenders by id, and two of the twelve invariants in this table did report offenders on their first run, so the instrument is known to fire rather than merely staying quiet. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: as a DECLARED invariant checked against live data, in the same table the ledger invariants live in - extended rather than given an eighth prover of its own. Each invariant names WHAT it compares and WHY that is the right comparison, because one wrong entry silently converts a real violation into a pass; this is the 'an exclusion must name its mechanism' discipline the order-totality gate already applies. Twelve invariants now run, ALL HOLD live, and the run carries a non-vacuity control (the trigger-linkage detector must see community_posts -> community_post_xp_awards, or a detector matching nothing would call every write pair on the platform unlinked). TWO OF THESE INVARIANTS WERE WRONG WHEN FIRST WRITTEN AND WERE CORRECTED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BANKED, both by reading the data rather than trusting the query. (1) 'a scope item is not completed twice', keyed on scope_item alone, reported 200 offenders - because a PM is RECURRING, so a monthly scope item legitimately carries a completion every month and the measured maximum is 12 distinct completion dates. A year of correct data read as a defect. Narrowing to the same DAY still reported 88, and those proved to have 2 or 3 DISTINCT workers at 2 or 3 DISTINCT timestamps - different people signing off the same item, not one write landing twice. The trigger-fires-once defect the oracle names looks like ONE worker at ONE instant with TWO rows, which is what the invariant now asks. (2) The orphan-hold check found one real offender and it is EXCLUDED BY ID WITH ITS REASON WRITTEN DOWN: reservation 39357091 holds part hd-bsk-1784479694 on 'Inventory Test Asset (H-scenario)', residue from a scenario walk whose part was removed, with neither consumed_at nor released_at set. It is a genuine dangling hold, it stays visible in the report, and excluding it keeps the gate able to catch a NEW orphan instead of being permanently red on known test debt. AND THE INVARIANTS THAT COULD NOT BE EXPRESSED WERE LEFT OWED RATHER THAN APPROXIMATED - notably 'original budget + sum of approved change orders = current budget', because `projects` stores only budget_php (the current figure) and no original, so there is nothing to compare against.

findings.detail: MOSTLY HOLDS, BUT WITH TWO REAL GAPS - recorded as a finding rather than a pass, because the second gap means the invariant cannot be enforced at all for a quarter of the ledger. MEASURED over 577 achievement_xp_log rows: exactly **1** duplicated source event - the same (worker_name, achievement_id, source_action, source_id) appearing twice, i.e. one action awarded XP twice. And **77 rows carry a NULL source_id**. THE 77 ARE THE BIGGER PROBLEM, and they are why this is not simply 'one duplicate to clean up': with no source_id there is no provenance, so those awards cannot be traced to the action that earned them and cannot be de-duplicated even in principle - a second award for the same underlying event is indistinguishable from a legitimate second event. A no-double-award invariant needs an identity for the awarding event; 77 rows do not have one. HOW THIS COMPOUNDS WHAT IS ALREADY RECORDED ON THIS PAGE: xp_total disagrees with sum(xp_earned) on 42 of 50 pairs (worst gap 349,711) and 32 log rows have no worker_achievements row at all. The duplicate and the 77 provenance-less rows are candidate contributors, though 1 duplicate cannot explain a gap of 349,711 - so they are part of the picture, not the whole of it. TO FINISH: make source_id NOT NULL with a unique index on (worker_name, achievement_id, source_action, source_id) so the database refuses a double award, then back-fill or quarantine the 77 before enabling it - the constraint cannot be added while rows exist that violate its premise.

findings.detail: NOT BANKED, BECAUSE THE ORACLE AS WRITTEN COMPARES TWO DIFFERENT CURRENCIES, and measuring it literally would have produced a spectacular false defect. MEASURED, live: this worker's ACHIEVEMENT XP sums to 390,064 across 4 achievements (uptime_guardian 266,979 · wrench_chronicle 96,463 · safety_sentinel 22,295 · parts_warden 4,327), while community_xp holds 0 for the same worker in this hive AND in every hive. Read as stated, the invariant fails by 390,064. ★BUT THEY ARE NOT THE SAME QUANTITY. achievement XP is earned against achievement_definitions and tracked in worker_achievements/achievement_xp_log; community_xp is a separate ledger earned by posting and answering. Nothing writes one from the other. Filing a 390,064-vs-0 defect would have been asserting that two independent currencies must be equal because the row's sentence puts them in one clause. ★AND THE PREMISE FAILS AT THE SURFACE TOO, which settles it: this page displays NO raw XP figure for the comparison to be made against. Its heroes are #ac-level-hero, #stat-composite (both 153, the SUM OF LEVELS, already banked green against v_worker_achievements_truth) and #stat-top (80). There is no achievements-page number that community_xp could agree or disagree with, so the oracle has no subject on this surface - the shape where a claim is asserted about something the page does not show. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it needs a decision rather than a probe: either (a) the row is rewritten to the claim that IS checkable and worth checking - that community_xp reads the same on community, hive and achievements WHERE EACH DISPLAYS IT - or (b) the platform genuinely intends one unified XP, in which case 390,064 vs 0 is a real and serious divergence and the fix is a product decision about which ledger is authoritative. I am not guessing which, because the two readings lead to opposite work. RELATED AND ALREADY SETTLED: this page's xp_is_ledger_sum row is green on a paired-write test in a rolled-back transaction, precisely because the seeded totals cannot be reconciled backwards - I re-derived that same 390,064-vs-2,230 gap here and found the bank had already recorded it as the premise of its own method rather than as a defect.

findings.detail: THE ORACLE IS MIS-SPECIFIED, AND THAT IS NOW SETTLED FROM THE RECORD RATHER THAN GUESSED. MEASURED first: this worker's ACHIEVEMENT XP sums to 390,064 across 4 achievements (uptime_guardian 266,979 · wrench_chronicle 96,463 · safety_sentinel 22,295 · parts_warden 4,327) while community_xp holds 0 for the same worker in this hive AND in every hive. Its purpose is the Community->Marketplace REPUTATION BRIDGE: community activity becomes portable, aggregate-only trust that the free marketplace turns into jobs. Achievement XP is a different currency entirely - earned against achievement_definitions, tracked in worker_achievements/achievement_xp_log, and its job is to drive levels and badges. Nothing writes either from the other, and nothing should. SO 390,064 vs 0 IS NOT A DIVERGENCE; it is two ledgers doing two jobs, and asserting they must be equal is asserting that a worker's posting reputation must equal their maintenance gamification score. ★AND THE PREMISE FAILS AT THE SURFACE INDEPENDENTLY, which is the second reason this cannot be banked either way: this page displays NO raw XP figure. Its heroes are #ac-level-hero and #stat-composite (both 153, the SUM OF LEVELS, already green against v_worker_achievements_truth) and #stat-top (80). There is no number here for community_xp to agree or disagree with. THE ROW STAYS OWED PENDING A RE-AUTHOR, not a product fix. evidence.asserts: every number rendered on the default view is named by its own element or an ancestor, so its meaning is available without leaving the surface
evidence.checked: MEASURED LIVE, read-only, with tools/prove_number_labelled.mjs (no clicks, no writes): 12 number-bearing element(s) on this page's default view, 12 labelled, 0 UNLABELLED, and the instrument's own control check passed (ctl=ok) so a page that could not detect a missing label would have reported itself rather than passing silently. 4 element(s) were excluded and the count is reported rather than hidden - identifiers like GEN-003 or '405 XP' read as numbers to a matcher but are names, so elements inside a link, a button, a table header, or carrying a data-* id are skipped. A 'number-bearing element' is defined narrowly: a LEAF element whose entire trimmed text is numeric after stripping currency, separators, % and a unit suffix - '9' and '61%' qualify, '9 open items carried over' does not because it labels itself. A label counts when it is non-numeric text of >=3 chars in the element's own aria-label/title or in an ancestor's text with the number removed, climbing at most 4 ancestors and only while that ancestor's subtree is section-sized or smaller (<=400 chars) - both bounds are load-bearing, because too tight invents defects (it once called analytics' fully-documented OEE hero unlabelled for being 35 chars too verbose) and too loose makes the pass free by accepting a whole section's prose as a label. TWO ORACLES, ONE TRUTH CONDITION - stated because it would be dishonest to present this as an independent second measurement. This bank's CM oracle `what_is_this_number` ('a person can state what the number means from the surface alone') is already green from this SAME instrument and this SAME reading; CE's `number_explained` asks 'a person can say what the number MEANS without leaving the surface'. Those are the same question in two lenses, so the same measurement settles both and no second walk was fabricated to make this row look separately earned. That two of the 200 slots ask one question is a FRAME observation, and it belongs to the roadmap's synthesis rather than to this row. SCOPE, precisely: this is V1 only. The prover walks the view each page OPENS ON, so the V2 row's second view (a modal, a sheet, a tab) is NOT covered by this reading and stays owed.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read. THE ORACLE MATTERS MORE THAN MOST UI TEXT: a source chip is a promise that a number came from named feeds, and a reader uses it to decide whether to trust the figure. A chip naming a feed the page never queried is worse than no chip, because it manufactures confidence. SO THE CLAIM IS CHECKED AGAINST THE NETWORK, not the source: every PostgREST /rest/v1/<relation> the view actually requests is captured at runtime, and each schema-shaped token the chip names must correspond to one. It is deliberately ONE-DIRECTIONAL - a chip that SUMMARISES is fine, a chip that INVENTS is not. ★TWO MANUFACTURED FINDINGS WERE CAUGHT AND REMOVED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS BANKED. The first version of the token test counted the bare word `logbook`, so asset-hub and analytics were both reported as naming an unread feed - on the strength of ordinary prose: 'Based on your asset records, risk scores, logbook, failure analysis'. That is a sentence describing FEATURES to a person, not an assertion about a table, and analytics is right on its own terms - it reads analytics_snapshots, a snapshot DERIVED from logbook data, which is precisely what 'saved snapshot ... based on your logbook' says. A keyword match over human prose is how a page's own helper text becomes a defect. The test now counts a token only when it is unmistakably schema-shaped (a v_ prefix, a _truth suffix, or a known table prefix + underscore); bare English words never qualify. ★AND THE VIEW IS READ INSIDE ITSELF. V1 is graded at page scope and V2 inside the OPENED view via the shared tools/dialog_targets.mjs registry, because crediting a V2 row with a V1 reading is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error this bank has already paid for once. NOT BANKED GREEN: this view displays NO source chip at all (0 on screen while the surface requested 8 relation(s)). A surface that makes no provenance claim has not made a TRUE one, and the oracle asks whether the claim is true - so silence cannot satisfy it. Scoring it green would credit the absence of a promise as a kept promise. THIS IS ALSO NOT AUTOMATICALLY A DEFECT. Most of the 23 are V2 dialogs - a composer, a confirm sheet, a detail panel - which display a form rather than a derived figure, and a provenance chip on a surface that states no number would be noise. WHAT SETTLES IT is the per-view question the bank actually asks: does THIS view show a figure a reader would want provenance for? If yes, the chip is missing and this is a real finding; if no, the row is declared-na under R10 with 'this view states no derived figure' as the reason and the CM comprehension oracles as its replacement. Left owed rather than guessed, because that question is per-view and answering it from a count would be inventing the verdict.

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_number_explained.mjs (new) - on the rendered page, in the view that owns the metric. ★NAMING IS NOT EXPLAINING, which is why this is a separate prover from prove_number_labelled.mjs. That one asks whether something adjacent NAMES the figure and the roster passes it 79/79. This asks whether a person can say what the number MEANS: 'PM compliance 61%%' is named and unexplained - 61%% of WHAT, over WHAT window, counted HOW? ★ONLY DERIVED FIGURES OWE AN EXPLANATION, and getting that wrong would redden every surface. A raw COUNT explains itself - 'Open Jobs 9' is nine jobs. A PERCENTAGE, RATE, SCORE, INDEX or COMPOSITE is computed from things the reader cannot see, and that is where the meaning lives off-screen. Any ONE of a denominator, a window, a derivation or a definition discharges the obligation; requiring all four would fail good surfaces. ★THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG THREE TIMES BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT, each caught by disbelieving the output: (1) EIGHTEEN abstentions on a platform that renders OEE and MTBF - analytics' KPI heroes live behind its phase panels, not the landing view, so the prover now reaches the view that owns the metric; (2) it failed hive's 'HEALTHY /100 composite risk - lower is better', a figure that states its scale AND its direction, because my denominator pattern demanded a digit on BOTH sides of the slash; (3) it failed project-report on 'Replace mechanical seal + bearings Leandro Mar... = 4.0' because the enclosing block resolved to a whole TABLE and every cell inherited the section's derived-ness - adjacency is not several hundred characters of table, so table cells are now excluded and long labels skipped. FOR THIS PAGE: no DERIVED figure rendered in the view measured - its numbers are raw counts, which explain themselves. Recorded as an ABSTENTION, not a pass: '0 unexplained of 0' reads identically to a thorough check, which is the vacuous green this bank refuses.

Its own comment records why - it once read retry_path:false / fallback:silentlyStale on a surface that handles both correctly, because closure-scoped loaders meant the page never moved, and it scored the UNCHANGED page. Every verdict banked here carries inductionLanded > 0 and inconclusive:false. ★AND THE LENS IS PROVEN ABLE TO PASS, so a FAIL is not a blanket instrument failure: across the roster it returned retry_path 3 PASS / 19 FAIL, rate_limit_legible 1/21, fallback_engaged 7/15, slow_honest 10/12. public-feed passes all four - consistent with its own history, since it is the page fixed so a failed read renders an error rather than 'No public posts yet'. RETRY PATH - FAILS, and the half that is certain is the half that matters. Under an injected 500 this page offers ZERO retry affordances: no 'try again', no 'reload', no 'refresh' control. That is confirmed TWO independent ways - the lens counted affordances:0, and a separate direct probe that 500'd every /rest/v1/ request and scanned the whole document for a retry control also found none. My direct probe, which failed EVERY read rather than the subset the lens induces, and which scanned the whole page rather than <main>, found that this page DOES say something failed under a total outage. So the page's failure MESSAGING may be better than the lens's number suggests - a partial induction can leave a surface half-populated and quiet. The missing retry CONTROL is not in doubt; the missing failure SENTENCE is, on this page. WHY IT IS NOT BANKED GREEN ANYWAY: the oracle asks for a retry PATH, and a failure a person cannot act on is the shape this family exists to catch - 'a failure that offers a retry which does not re-attempt is worse than one that offers none', and offering none at all is the floor of that same scale.

findings.title: The DB's legible rate-limit message is likely MASKED by a generic client string on the write path
findings.detail: The refusal this row banks on is excellent AT ITS SOURCE: 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' with HINT logbook_daily_user. But the client does not necessarily show it. logbook.html:1885 renders save failures as a fixed string - 'Could not save. Check your connection and try again.' - which is not only generic but WRONG for this case: the connection is fine, the person hit a daily cap, and 'try again' is the one instruction guaranteed to fail until midnight. So the platform can produce a genuinely good limit message and still tell the reader to retry immediately. This is the mirror image of a defect fixed earlier in this same session, where pages echoed the RAW upstream message to the reader: the lesson is not 'always show the server string' nor 'never show it', but that a write path needs to distinguish a LIMIT (legible, actionable, has a reset time) from a FAULT (retry may work) - and the HINT key exists precisely so it can. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE on this row because the oracle asks whether the rate limit is legible, and at the layer that produces it, it is - verifiably, with a machine-readable key. TO FINISH: on the write error path, branch on the hint/SQLSTATE (logbook_daily_user, 54000) and surface the server's own sentence plus its reset time instead of the connection string. Then re-walk this oracle at the client layer.

evidence.asserts: when a limit is hit the refusal is legible - it names the limit, the scope, and when it clears, and carries a machine-readable key so a client can tell WHICH limit fired
evidence.checked: FIRED FOR REAL, NOT READ FROM THE SOURCE - and then the source was read to confirm the second tier. Inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK as an authenticated member (role SET, not just claims), a burst of 400 logbook inserts was attempted. The trigger refused with: **'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.'** carrying HINT 'logbook_daily_user'. Verified clean afterwards: 0 probe rows survived the rollback. findings.detail: FAILS, MEASURED DECISIVELY: **achievements writes `0` into its KPI heroes while the reads are still pending, then replaces them with the real values.** With 8 reads held in flight and 0 resolved, the observer recorded 25 numeric writes including `ac-week-hero` = 0, `ac-active-hero` = 0 and `ac-level-hero` = 0. After the reads resolved, 14 further writes landed - `ac-level-hero` = 153, `stat-composite` = 153, `stat-top` = 80. SO THE ZEROS ARE ASSERTIONS, NOT PLACEHOLDERS, and that is exactly the distinction the three other pages in this pass passed on: index wrote only decorative stage numbers in flight, project-manager and community only the local offline-queue badge, and all three deferred their real figures until the data arrived. achievements did not - the render reached those elements first and stamped a zero into them. WHY IT MATTERS ON THIS PAGE SPECIFICALLY: a level of 0 and 'this week 0' are not neutral - they are a claim that the worker has earned nothing, on the surface whose entire purpose is recognising what they have earned. The true value was 153. Someone opening this page on a slow connection sees themselves at zero. AND IT COMPOUNDS THE XP DEFECT ALREADY RECORDED HERE: this page's stored xp_total already disagrees with its own ledger on 42 of 50 pairs (worst gap 349,711), with 32 orphan log rows and 77 rows lacking a source_id. So the number is both wrong at rest AND briefly zero on the way in. The loading fix is independent and small; the ledger fix is the migration-level one. TO FINISH (batched per A15): do not write to `ac-*-hero` until the read resolves - render the skeleton the platform already uses (alert-hub holds 6 skeleton elements and ZERO bare numbers during the wait, the reference behaviour), or write the dash sentinel. Then re-walk. MEASURED BY DETECTING THE WRITE, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL THAT MAKES A ZERO MEANINGFUL. Reads are wrapped in a 5s delay and counted on resolution; a MutationObserver on documentElement records every mutation whose resulting text is purely numeric, stamped with how many reads had resolved at that instant. So 'did the page write a number before it had the data?' is a measured fact. THE CONTROL IS NOT OPTIONAL, AND TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS PROBE PROVE WHY. Version 1 tested only the ADDED NODE's own text, so a render that sets innerHTML on a container (numeric leaf nested inside) recorded nothing. Version 2 fixed that and STILL recorded nothing - because addInitScript runs at document start when `document.documentElement` can be null, so `observe()` threw and the observer never attached. Both versions reported **0 writes on pages that visibly populated**, i.e. a flattering zero produced entirely by a broken instrument. Version 3 attaches on a poller AND writes its own numeric sentinel ('4242') that the observer must see; if that control fails the reading is REFUSED rather than reported. All four pages here returned controlOK = true. A ZERO FROM AN UNATTACHED OBSERVER IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM AN HONEST PAGE - which is the whole reason the control exists.

findings.title: The DB's legible rate-limit message is likely MASKED by a generic client string on the write path
findings.detail: The refusal this row banks on is excellent AT ITS SOURCE: 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' with HINT logbook_daily_user. But the client does not necessarily show it. logbook.html:1885 renders save failures as a fixed string - 'Could not save. Check your connection and try again.' - which is not only generic but WRONG for this case: the connection is fine, the person hit a daily cap, and 'try again' is the one instruction guaranteed to fail until midnight. So the platform can produce a genuinely good limit message and still tell the reader to retry immediately. This is the mirror image of a defect fixed earlier in this same session, where pages echoed the RAW upstream message to the reader: the lesson is not 'always show the server string' nor 'never show it', but that a write path needs to distinguish a LIMIT (legible, actionable, has a reset time) from a FAULT (retry may work) - and the HINT key exists precisely so it can. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE on this row because the oracle asks whether the rate limit is legible, and at the layer that produces it, it is - verifiably, with a machine-readable key. TO FINISH: on the write error path, branch on the hint/SQLSTATE (logbook_daily_user, 54000) and surface the server's own sentence plus its reset time instead of the connection string. Then re-walk this oracle at the client layer.

WHICH OF THE GATE'S CHECKS PROVE THIS ORACLE (named, not inherited from 'the gate is green'): OBJECT-level access: the gate's cross-tenant READ and OWN-SCOPE WRITE checks - read_logbook_xhive and read_cxp_xhive (a FOREIGN hive's v_logbook_truth and community_xp return ZERO rows) and logbook_edit_ownscope (a member cannot UPDATE another hive's logbook entry). findings.title: auth_uid is bound from the JWT, but the display column worker_name is stored exactly as the body supplied it
findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. Writing as Hector (JWT sub 8fb252f7-...) while supplying auth_uid = Romeo's id AND worker_name = 'Romeo Beltran': the stored auth_uid was corrected to Hector's by trg_bind_submitter_logbook, and the stored worker_name remained 'Romeo Beltran'. So the authoritative identity is safe and the human-readable one is not. WHY THAT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY, RATHER THAN AS A PURIST POINT: reads across this platform filter and group by worker_name, not by auth_uid - `.eq('worker_name', WORKER_NAME)` is the dominant pattern in logbook, inventory, dayplanner, skillmatrix and the resume evidence path. So a row whose worker_name disagrees with its auth_uid is attributed to the WRONG PERSON in every list that reads it, while looking perfectly consistent to any check that only inspects auth_uid. logbook is the platform's evidence base: it feeds MTBF, PM compliance and a person's resume evidence, so misattribution is not cosmetic. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE because the oracle asks whether identity comes from the JWT rather than the body, and for the identity column it does. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. The first is the smaller change and keeps the existing read patterns working.

findings.detail: FAILS at the transport layer, and the obligation lands on this page: 1 of its 1 probed relation(s) return the SAME 200 and the same array body to an anon caller as to a member - achievement_xp_log (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows). TO FINISH: this page must decide refusal-vs-absence from SESSION STATE rather than from the response, and its empty state must not claim 'nothing here' when the real answer is 'not signed in'. Of this page's 4 read relation(s), 1 were probed live at the gateway (achievement_xp_log).  THE MEASURED FINDING, which is about the CONTRACT rather than a bug: on 26 of the 40 relations a REFUSAL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ABSENCE. An anonymous caller and an authenticated member receive the SAME status (200) and the same body TYPE (a JSON array), differing only in row count - anon 0 rows, member 2. A request with NO apikey at all also returns 200 []. So nothing in the response separates 'you are not permitted', 'you are not signed in', and 'this hive genuinely has no entries'. This is PostgREST + RLS by construction - row filtering is not request refusal - so it is not a gateway defect. It is an OBLIGATION every surface inherits: the client must decide from session state, and a page that does not will render an expired session as an empty plant. That is the read-path half of the 401-vs-403 lesson this platform already carries. The counter-example proves the point: some relations answer a refusal with 42501, a code a client can act on. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted.

Writing as Hector (JWT sub 8fb252f7-...) while supplying auth_uid = Romeo's id AND worker_name = 'Romeo Beltran': the stored auth_uid was corrected to Hector's by trg_bind_submitter_logbook, and the stored worker_name remained 'Romeo Beltran'. So the authoritative identity is safe and the human-readable one is not. WHY THAT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY, RATHER THAN AS A PURIST POINT: reads across this platform filter and group by worker_name, not by auth_uid - `.eq('worker_name', WORKER_NAME)` is the dominant pattern in logbook, inventory, dayplanner, skillmatrix and the resume evidence path. So a row whose worker_name disagrees with its auth_uid is attributed to the WRONG PERSON in every list that reads it, while looking perfectly consistent to any check that only inspects auth_uid. logbook is the platform's evidence base: it feeds MTBF, PM compliance and a person's resume evidence, so misattribution is not cosmetic. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE because the oracle asks whether identity comes from the JWT rather than the body, and for the identity column it does. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. The first is the smaller change and keeps the existing read patterns working.

findings.detail: FAILS at the transport layer, and the obligation lands on this page: 1 of its 1 probed relation(s) return the SAME 200 and the same array body to an anon caller as to a member - achievement_xp_log (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows). TO FINISH: this page must decide refusal-vs-absence from SESSION STATE rather than from the response, and its empty state must not claim 'nothing here' when the real answer is 'not signed in'. Of this page's 4 read relation(s), 1 were probed live at the gateway (achievement_xp_log).  THE MEASURED FINDING, which is about the CONTRACT rather than a bug: on 26 of the 40 relations a REFUSAL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ABSENCE. An anonymous caller and an authenticated member receive the SAME status (200) and the same body TYPE (a JSON array), differing only in row count - anon 0 rows, member 2. A request with NO apikey at all also returns 200 []. So nothing in the response separates 'you are not permitted', 'you are not signed in', and 'this hive genuinely has no entries'. This is PostgREST + RLS by construction - row filtering is not request refusal - so it is not a gateway defect. It is an OBLIGATION every surface inherits: the client must decide from session state, and a page that does not will render an expired session as an empty plant. That is the read-path half of the 401-vs-403 lesson this platform already carries. The counter-example proves the point: some relations answer a refusal with 42501, a code a client can act on. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted.

scenarios.oracle: each achievement states its criteria

evidence.asserts: each achievement states what earns it, in the imperative, on the tile itself
evidence.checked: Walked live as the signed-in worker; read-only, nothing awarded or written. Achievements carry their criteria as an instruction rather than a description - 'Reach Level 50 in any 5 domains to unlock' sits on the tile it governs, so a person reads WHAT TO DO, not merely what they lack. The domain tiles do the same in miniature by naming the activity that feeds them ('Logbook entry submitted', 'Wrench Chronicle', 'Uptime Guardian', 'Parts Warden'), and the page's source chip defines every headline metric it shows: 'XP this week: points earned in the last 7 days - Total level: your levels added up across all domains (max 1,200 = 12 domains x level 100) - Active domains: domains where you have reached level 1 or higher'. That last one matters for this row: a criterion that uses a term the page invented ('active domains') is only a criterion if the term is defined, and it is, in the same chip.
evidence.value_checked: 'Locked · Reach Level 50 in any 5 domains to unlock'; domain tiles 'Wrench Chronicle', 'Uptime Guardian', 'Parts Warden', 'Logbook entry submitted'; chip defines XP this week / Total level / Active domains.

subject.name: XP per action is stated before the action

scenarios.oracle: XP per action is stated before the action, where it is meant to motivate

evidence.asserts: FIXED THIS WALK. The oracle asks that XP per action be stated BEFORE the action, since that is the only point at which it can motivate. The page previously named exactly one rate, and only inside a recommendation shown after the fact ('that earns +100 XP in the Failure Hunter domain'); every other rate lived solely in trigger source nobody using the product can read. I did not invent a price list - I extracted the rates the platform actually awards and published those, so the page cannot drift from the economy it describes: log an entry 20 (+20 when problem, action and knowledge exceed 200 characters); close a job 50 (+30 root cause, +15 machine and downtime hours, +25 within 24 hours, up to 120); breakdown closed with root cause 100; safety entry 60; PM completion 60; community post 20 (+40 if safety); skill badge 250, the largest single award; calculator run 40; shift plan published 40; team member added 50. It went into the existing 'How XP and tiers work' explainer rather than a new panel, which is where a reader already goes to understand XP. Two honest riders sit under it: XP is not money and buys nothing, and XP is taken back if the work behind it is deleted - the latter being true only as of this same walk, when migration 61 gave logbook XP its reversal.
evidence.checked: Read the rates out of the shipped triggers rather than from any document, since a published rate that disagrees with the code is worse than none. Eight came from a regex over award_achievement_xp calls in every trg_%achievement_xp function; three more (logbook_submit, logbook_close, community_post) pass a VARIABLE rather than a literal and were invisible to that regex, so they were read from the function bodies directly - which is also where the conditional bonuses and their exact triggering conditions came from, so the published bonus text states what actually earns it. Cross-checked against the one rate the page already cited: its '+100 XP Failure Hunter' matches breakdown_root_cause=100. The insert is static body markup, not a template literal, so no interpolation risk.
evidence.value_checked: logbook_submit 20 (+20 >200 chars) | logbook_close 50 (+30 root_cause, +15 machine+downtime_hours, +25 <24h) | breakdown_root_cause 100 | safety_entry 60 | detailed_entry 20 | pm_complete 60 | community_post 20 (+40 safety) | calc_run 40 | shift_publish 40 | team_lead 50 | skill_badge_earned 250 | pre-existing page citation '+100 XP Failure Hunter' agrees with source

evidence.asserts: progress states how much REMAINS in the same unit it is earned in, per domain

seen.ref: silver 11 / gold 51 set by WorkHive (the enforcing trigger, per the marketplace BI walk) + achievements.html:836

scenarios.oracle: provider tier thresholds (silver 11, gold 51) and who sets them are stated

evidence.asserts: Thresholds were already stated well; the AUTHORITY was missing and is now stated. The block tells a provider exactly how far they are from the next tier - 'N more completed jobs reach Silver', 'N more jobs and a 4.5 star average reach Gold' - which is better than a static table because it is the distance THEY have left, and the numbers are the same ones the view computes with (>= 10 jobs for silver; >= 25 plus rating >= 4.5 for gold). What it never said is WHO decides. On a standing that governs who gets first look at paid hails, 'is this earned or granted?' is the question a provider actually has, and the answer is favourable: v_service_provider_truth COMPUTES the tier from verified completions and rating, with no stored counter anyone can set by hand. The block now says so. NOTE FOR THE ROADMAP: its parenthetical 'silver 11, gold 51' does not match the shipped rule, which is silver at 10 jobs and gold at 25 jobs with a 4.5 rating - the roadmap text is stale, the page and the view agree with each other.
evidence.checked: The stated numbers were compared against the view's own CASE expression rather than against the roadmap's parenthetical, which is what exposed the roadmap as the stale one. The authority claim was verified before being written: v_service_provider_truth derives tier in SQL and marketplace_sellers.tier - the stored column the marketplace listings read - is a different field entirely, so 'not granted by hand' is true of the figure THIS page shows. scenarios.oracle: XP is not money, and nothing on the surface implies it is

evidence.asserts: nothing on the surface implies XP is currency - no monetary word, symbol, or redemption affordance appears anywhere

findings.title: TRACED: the .wh-avatar overflow is the avatar's OWN centred text, not the level badge - and it is a consequence of this session's overflow:visible fix
findings.detail: THREE PROBES, AND THE FIRST TWO WERE WRONG - recording the chain because the wrong answers were the plausible ones. (1) I assumed the badge: .wh-avatar-lvl is positioned bottom:-8px to hang below the circle and the avatar had overflow:hidden, so the two rules fought. That WAS a real defect - 21% of every level pill clipped across 32 avatars, digits cut - and fixing it (mask moved to .wh-avatar > img, container set to overflow:visible) was correct and is verified: 0 pills clipped on community and achievements. (2) I then assumed the badge also explained the horizontal scrollWidth excess and widened my probe's absolute-child exclusion to DESCENDANTS. That made the readings WORSE - community 14 -> 22, achievements 11 -> 20 - because the badge is centred with translateX(-50%) and never passes the avatar's right edge: measured layout box right edge 61 against clientWidth 64 (3px INSIDE), painted box right edge 48. I reverted it rather than add a third guess. (3) THE DECISIVE TEST, which should have been first: remove the suspect and see if the symptom goes. Hiding the pill, removing only its transform, and pulling it fully inside vertically ALL left scrollWidth 84 against clientWidth 64 - a 20px excess completely unchanged in every case. So the badge contributes nothing to it. THE ACTUAL CAUSE: .wh-avatar is `display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center` with its initials as a direct text node. A centred flex item wider than its container overflows EQUALLY ON BOTH SIDES, so text ~104px wide in a 64px content box spills ~20px each way and scrollWidth reads 64 + 20 = 84 - which is exactly the measurement. The excess is the avatar's own label being wider than the circle. AND THIS IS A SIDE EFFECT OF MY OWN FIX, stated plainly rather than left for someone to find: under the previous overflow:hidden those oversized initials were CLIPPED to the circle; under overflow:visible they now SPILL outside it. Both the badge and the text were sharing one overflow property for opposite purposes, and no single value satisfies both. TO CLOSE, and it needs a look at the rendering rather than another measurement: identify which avatars actually carry oversized labels (the sample here shows initials like 'PA' fitting and glyph labels like the star tier badges running wide), then constrain the LABEL - a max-width with a smaller font-size or a single-glyph cap - so the text fits the circle while the badge keeps hanging below it. Constraining the text is the fix; putting the clip back would re-break the badge.
findings.observed: avatar clientWidth 64 / scrollWidth 84 / excess 20, unchanged with the pill hidden, un-transformed, or moved inside; pill layout right edge 61 vs clientWidth 64

findings.title: RESOLVED - NOT A DEFECT: the .wh-avatar overflow is a decorative spinning tier halo drawn by a PSEUDO-ELEMENT, structurally invisible to any DOM walk
findings.detail: FOUR PROBES, AND THE FIRST THREE WERE WRONG. Recording the whole chain because the wrong answers were each more plausible than the right one, and the shape of the error is the lesson. GUESS 1 - the level badge. .wh-avatar-lvl is positioned bottom:-8px to hang below the circle while the avatar had overflow:hidden, so the two rules fought. That WAS a real defect and the fix stands, verified: 21% of every level pill had been clipped across 32 avatars, and 0 are clipped now. But it did not explain the horizontal excess. GUESS 2 - the badge again, via my probe. I widened the absolute-child exclusion to DESCENDANTS to absorb it, and the readings got WORSE: community 14 -> 22, achievements 11 -> 20. Measured, the badge's layout box ends at 61 against clientWidth 64 - three pixels INSIDE - and its painted box at 48. Reverted. GUESS 3 - the avatar's own centred text. .wh-avatar is display:flex with justify-content:center, and a centred flex item wider than its box overflows equally BOTH ways, which would make scrollWidth = clientWidth + 2x the spill. Arithmetically perfect and factually wrong: the initials 'PA' measure 21px in a 64px box via a Range, and 0 of 20 avatars have text wider than their container. THE DECISIVE TEST, which should have been probe 1: remove the suspect and re-read. Hiding the pill, removing its transform, and pulling it inside all left the excess UNCHANGED at 20px - so the badge was exonerated by measurement long before I stopped blaming it. Then, forcing `content: none` on both pseudo-elements took scrollWidth from 91 to EXACTLY 64 = clientWidth. THE CAUSE: .wh-tier-legend::after is an 84x84 ring at inset:-10px with animation wh-spin, plus a 72x72 ::before, on a 72px avatar - a decorative rotating halo marking the top tier. It is intentional, it is aria-invisible, and it is a PSEUDO-ELEMENT, so no querySelectorAll('*') walk can ever see it. That is why three rounds of DOM reasoning failed: I was looking for the contributor among elements, and the contributor is not an element. VERDICT: THERE IS NO OVERFLOW DEFECT ON THESE PAGES. The rows stay owed only because the probe needs a fifth exclusion - skip a self-overflow whose excess disappears when ::before/::after content is suppressed - and that exclusion must be written and self-tested, not assumed. THE TRANSFERABLE RULE: scrollWidth is a rendering fact, not a DOM fact. Before attributing it to any element, test by SUBTRACTION - remove the candidate and see whether the number moves. A DOM walk cannot see pseudo-elements, generated content, or a transformed paint box, so reasoning from the element tree will confidently name the wrong culprit.
findings.observed: wh-tier-legend: clientWidth 64, scrollWidth 91 (excess 27) -> 64 with ::before/::after content suppressed. ::after 84x84 inset:-10px animation wh-spin; ::before 72x72 inset:-4px. findings.title: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing. ★WHY A VIEW-SCOPED PROVER HAD TO BE BUILT FOR THIS: a page-level sweep of all 22 pages (tools/prove_page_contrast.mjs) found the platform clean and settled NOTHING here, because every owed contrast row in these banks is authored against V2 or V3 - the dialogs - while their V1 siblings were already green. Banking a page-default reading onto a V2 row is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error that has already put 14 rows in this bank carrying another view's verdict. The view is opened through tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the same shared registry ten other provers use, so the view graded here is the view they grade. WCAG 2.x is measured with the composited probe: the background is blended UP the ancestor chain, because a translucent tint over a dark card is not the colour the stylesheet names, and text over a gradient is recorded as UNMEASURABLE rather than being compared against a canvas it never sits on - the shape that once reported ratio exactly 1.00 for perfectly legible text. NOT BANKED: this view yielded ZERO measurable samples (30 unmeasurable), so there is no denominator and a pass would be vacuous. The cause is structural rather than a probe fault, and it was verified by tracing the paint chain: the dialog's inner card is a TRANSLUCENT GRADIENT - linear-gradient(145deg, rgba(42,61,88,0.6) ...) - over a rgba(0,0,0,0.75) scrim over the page. WCAG 2.x is a ratio between TWO colours, and there is no single background colour here to be the second one. THE APCA SIBLING OF THIS ROW IS NOT AFFECTED and was measured normally, because that lens averages the gradient's stops instead of demanding one flat colour - which is why the platform treats APCA as the primary contrast oracle on this dark shell. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: sample the RENDERED PIXELS around each glyph from a screenshot of this view, which is the only way to obtain the real second colour behind text that sits on a gradient. That is a buildable instrument, not a ceiling - it is simply not built yet, and this row stays owed until it is.

findings.title: NOT BANKED, BECAUSE THE PASS IS VACUOUS ON THIS VIEW - and the prover's own numbers are what show it.
findings.detail: NOT BANKED, BECAUSE THE PASS IS VACUOUS ON THIS VIEW - and the prover's own numbers are what show it. tools/prove_dialog_a11y.mjs graded 36 of 43 registry targets with ZERO failing, and its summary line reads 'every focusable control shows a causally-verified focus indicator'. On this view that sentence is true the way any statement about an empty set is true: the report records focus.candidates = 0 and focus.checked = 0. No focusable control was examined, so nothing about focus indication was established. Banking it green would put a row in the bank whose evidence is an empty denominator - the exact false green this bank exists to prevent. THIS IS A PROPERTY OF THE VIEW, NOT A DEFECT. Six of the thirty-six graded views hold no focusable controls at all - engineering-design's guide tab, shift-brain's verdict summary and its details disclosure, report-sender's contacts list, public-feed's feed list, achievements' recent list. They are READ surfaces: text, cards and figures. A view with nothing to focus cannot fail a focus oracle, and it cannot pass one either. WORTH SEPARATING FROM THE SIBLING ORACLES, because they are NOT vacuous here: this same run measured accessible names and reduced-motion on the same views and those are real readings - a name applies to any control, focusable or not, and 'nothing animates under prefers-reduced-motion' is a statement about the whole subtree. So the a11y run is only empty for FOCUS on these six. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THIS ROW: either the view genuinely gains an interactive control (then re-run and grade it), or the row is dispositioned declared-na with this reason under R10 - which needs a replacement oracle named, and the honest replacement is that the view is READABLE and its figures are labelled (CL contrast + CM what_is_this_number), not that its focus ring works. AND AN INSTRUMENT NOTE, since the prover is otherwise strong: its per-view PASS does not distinguish 'checked N controls, all good' from 'checked none'. The distinction is recoverable only from focus.candidates in the report, so a consumer that reads the exit code alone would bank all six of these as proven. The count belongs in the printed line.

And where a Tab walk reaches nothing inside a non-trapping dialog, focus is SEEDED ON THE CONTAINER and the walk repeated, with `seeded` recorded, because three views once reported 'candidates: 2, checked: 0, noRing: []' - a green summary over a walk that examined nothing. findings.detail: FAILS: with 11 of this page's reads answered 403/42501, it shows only a GENERIC error ("Skip to main content ℹ Achievements failed to load.") - the person is told it broke, never that they are not allowed.  WHAT THIS ORACLE IS REALLY FOR, and the good news first: it checks that a refusal names PERMISSION rather than IDENTITY, because this platform has already shipped that exact inversion - a 42501 rendered as 'your session has expired', which sends a signed-IN person to re-authenticate for a problem authentication cannot fix, and 401/403 collapsed into one message so neither audience got a true statement. ZERO of the 16 graded pages made that mistake on this run. utils.js:1607 whIsAuthFailure() is why: it returns FALSE for status 403 with the comment 'authenticated, and refused. Not a session problem', and documents 42501 as insufficient_privilege. That discrimination is holding. HOW THE REFUSAL WAS INDUCED, and why it is the real branch: every Supabase REST read is answered with the body PostgREST actually sends for a row-level-security refusal - HTTP 403 with {"code":"42501","message":"permission denied for table"} - so the page's own error handling takes the same path it would in production. The patch is on window.fetch, NOT page.route, because a warm service worker serves from cache and bypasses route interception; it is installed with addInitScript in a context closed after each page so it cannot leak. NON-WRITING: it makes a READ return 403. THE INJECTION PROVES ITSELF: every intercepted call increments a counter, and a page where the counter is zero is UNGRADED rather than judged. That guard exists because the first version of this prover silently did nothing - a regex written inside a template literal collapsed to one that terminates at its second character, so the init script was a SyntaxError, every read succeeded normally, and the prover reported 'the reads were all refused and the page said nothing' while nothing had been refused at all. Hit counts on this run ranged from 8 to 42 per page. AND THE SIGNAL MUST APPEAR: the same page is read WITHOUT the injection first, and if its ordinary copy already matches the refusal vocabulary the page is UNGRADED - which is exactly what happened to skillmatrix, whose normal text contains a matching phrase. Without that control a page whose everyday copy happens to say 'cannot' would pass for free. THE SYNTHESIS - THIS IS ONE MISSING SURFACE, NOT 15 PAGE BUGS. Of 16 graded pages: 13 said NOTHING AT ALL when every read was refused, 2 showed only a GENERIC error ('Analysis failed, check console'; 'Achievements failed to load.'), and 1 passed. The platform already has the pieces - a central WRITE-failure message and the correct 401-vs-403 discriminator in utils.js - but there is no equivalent on the READ path, so a refused read renders as dashes or blanks with no explanation. On logbook the numbers '516 entries 30 machines 6 open' became '- entries - machines - open' with the body text identical to the character (1107 before and after) and not one word about why. A person cannot tell 'there is no data' from 'the load failed' from 'you are not allowed', and those three call for three different actions. THE FIX IS ONE ADOPTION, not 15 edits: give the read path the same treatment the write path already has. This independently reproduces a finding already recorded as 'the message already exists; the gap is ADOPTION on the read path'. SCOPE: V1, the page as it loads, and READ refusal only - a refused WRITE is a different path with its own central message, and is not claimed here. 5 of the 22 pages are excluded from the sweep because they are public or have no authenticated read to refuse. The walk is NON-WRITING.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.
