evidence.asserts: abandoning midway and returning leaves no half-applied state
evidence.checked: DECLARED-NA WITH A NAMED REPLACEMENT (rail R10), AND THE REASON IS THE ORACLE'S OWN WORD: MIDWAY. This oracle asks what happens when someone abandons PART-WAY THROUGH. On this page the person-caused action is nothing at all - its XP and badges are awarded server-side by triggers and RPCs - there is no part-way. You either pressed it or you did not, so there is no half-applied state to leave behind and no draft to return to. ★WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN PASSED: 'no half-applied state' over an action with no middle is VACUOUSLY TRUE, and a vacuous truth banked as a live-walk PASS is how coverage improves by deleting obligations. Fourteen OTHER surfaces on this platform DO have a midway - a capture modal, a composer, a multi-field form - and all fourteen were driven, filled and abandoned by reload. This page is not one of them, and the emptiness is the finding. ★THE REPLACEMENT, so the surface is not simply excused: what this page owes instead is that the effect its one press DOES cause is observable to the person who caused it - carried by effect_visible, already proven green here (PB-achievements-072-CF-ufai-F-V1-effect_visible). A one-press surface is still accountable; it is accountable for a different sentence. ★AND ONE PAGE WAS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED FROM THIS DISPOSITION: skillmatrix has no green effect_visible, because its exam could not be reached (SKILL_CONTENT is module-scoped and no discipline/level pair produced questions). Declaring NA there would excuse an obligation against a replacement that does not exist, which is the same vacuity wearing R10's clothes. Its rows stay owed with that diagnosis.

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

evidence.checked: DECLARED-NA WITH A NAMED REPLACEMENT (rail R10), AND THE REASON IS THE ORACLE'S OWN WORD: MIDWAY. This oracle asks what happens when someone abandons PART-WAY THROUGH. On this page the person-caused action is nothing at all - its XP and badges are awarded server-side by triggers and RPCs - there is no part-way. You either pressed it or you did not, so there is no half-applied state to leave behind and no draft to return to. ★WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN PASSED: 'no half-applied state' over an action with no middle is VACUOUSLY TRUE, and a vacuous truth banked as a live-walk PASS is how coverage improves by deleting obligations. Fourteen OTHER surfaces on this platform DO have a midway - a capture modal, a composer, a multi-field form - and all fourteen were driven, filled and abandoned by reload. This page is not one of them, and the emptiness is the finding. ★THE REPLACEMENT, so the surface is not simply excused: what this page owes instead is that the effect its one press DOES cause is observable to the person who caused it - carried by effect_visible, already proven green here (PB-achievements-072-CF-ufai-F-V1-effect_visible). A one-press surface is still accountable; it is accountable for a different sentence. ★AND ONE PAGE WAS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED FROM THIS DISPOSITION: skillmatrix has no green effect_visible, because its exam could not be reached (SKILL_CONTENT is module-scoped and no discipline/level pair produced questions). Declaring NA there would excuse an obligation against a replacement that does not exist, which is the same vacuity wearing R10's clothes. Its rows stay owed with that diagnosis.

findings.detail: FAILS: UNEXPLAINED — still renders 6 of 9 number(s) non-zero (5 of them also present signed-in, which may be static furniture: 18 .wh-avatar-lvl; 38 .wh-avatar-lvl; 63 .wh-avatar-lvl) and nothing on screen says the data could not be loaded. With a session this view rendered 14 non-zero value(s) over 2429 characters; with the auth token removed from storage it rendered 6 over 1698, and the page did not redirect, did not add a sign-in prompt it was not already showing, and did not state that anything failed to load. What is on screen after the kill: "Skip to main content Growth ← Skills Achievements Live · refreshed on load · Based on your achievements, XP history & worker · XP this week: points earned in the last 7 d".  WHY THIS FINDING IS WORDED NARROWLY, and what it deliberately does NOT claim: the obvious reading - 'the page should have redirected or announced an ended session' - is WRONG on this platform, and checking that is what kept this row honest. index.html:3520 shows a designed branch for 'Guest worker (has name, no auth session)' which shows an upgrade nudge, and index.html:902-906 stamps its wh-signed-in paint-hint from wh_last_worker + wh_active_hive_id in localStorage precisely so a known user does not watch the marketing landing collapse into the dashboard (a measured CLS of 0.24). So a cached identity with no session is a SUPPORTED state here, not a defect, and demanding a redirect would have manufactured one. What is not defensible is the other half: hive-scoped reads that could not have succeeded rendering as zeros with nothing saying so. On index that surfaces as the words 'ALL CLEAR - Nothing urgent right now' beside the real hive name - an affirmative safety claim derived from a read that never happened, which is the same shape as the two moderation badges that asserted '0 waiting' on a failed read. HOW IT WAS MEASURED, live, and what the oracle deliberately is NOT: it is not 'does the page redirect to sign-in'. Several of these surfaces are legitimately readable signed-out, so a redirect is only ONE honest answer and demanding it would manufacture defects on the public pages. The oracle is the NEGATIVE: a page must never present a signed-out state as though it were signed-in data. Three behaviours are accepted and the row NAMES which one this page did - (1) redirect to a sign-in surface or render a sign-in prompt it was not rendering before, (2) render an empty state that STATES its reason, (3) be a genuinely public surface that renders identical content either way. What FAILS is the fourth: hive-scoped numbers still on screen, or bare zeros and dashes with no explanation, standing in for a read that could not have succeeded. THE SESSION IS KILLED IN localStorage, NOT IN COOKIES, and that detail is the difference between a real measurement and a vacuous one: supabase-js persists the session as sb-<project-ref>-auth-token in localStorage, so clearing cookies would leave the page fully signed in and the probe would measure nothing while reporting a pass. Every sb-* / auth-token / supabase key in BOTH localStorage and sessionStorage is swept (hardcoding one project ref is the other way this goes silently vacuous), then the page is RELOADED so the client re-reads storage from cold. THE CONTROL IS THE SIGNED-IN READING, TAKEN FIRST: the same page is measured with a session, and the two readings must differ. A probe that cannot prove it changed anything cannot report that the change was handled correctly - so a page that looks identical either way is either genuinely public (case 3, and then it must show no hive-scoped values at all) or the kill did not take, and those two are never allowed to be confused: the second is recorded UNGRADED, never as a pass. TWO FALSE READINGS WERE CAUGHT AND FIXED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BANKED, and both are why this row is trustworthy. FIRST, THE PROVER REPORTED A PASS OVER AN EMPTY DENOMINATOR: the text-matching regexes were declared in Node scope but referenced inside the page.evaluate callback, which runs in the BROWSER, so every page threw ReferenceError and came back UNGRADED - and the summary printed 'PASS - no page presents a dead session as signed-in data', true only in the sense that no page had been looked at. Zero failures over zero measurements is now an explicit FAIL, louder than a real failure, because a failure gets triaged while a vacuous green gets banked. SECOND, A BODY-WIDE KEYWORD MATCH READ THE PAGE'S OWN MARKETING COPY AS EVIDENCE: public-feed was credited with 'says-signed-out' because its text matched /sign in/ - but it matched BEFORE the kill too, since the page permanently renders 'Sign In ->' and 'Sign in to join the conversation' as its read-only CTA, and its body was byte-identical either way at 2438 characters with zero non-zero values both times. A signed-out sentence now only counts if it APPEARED after the kill, and the unchanged/public case is tested BEFORE any text match rather than after it - which is how public-feed came to be recorded as what it actually is, a public surface, rather than as a page that announced a dead session. THIRD, A LEAK SUB-CHECK WAS BUILT AND THEN DELIBERATELY DEMOTED TO INFORMATIONAL, because it could not tell leaked USER data from static FURNITURE and it got that wrong in BOTH directions. Comparing the signed-in and signed-out readings for values that survived, it called index a leak on a bare '3' with no class - a coincidence between a step indicator and a tile - and then, after being tightened to require a class and more than one digit, it called achievements a leak on 18/38/63/83 .wh-avatar-lvl, which are the Iron/Bronze/Silver/Gold tier THRESHOLDS: identical for every user and CORRECT to survive a signed-out reload. Telling those apart requires knowing which numbers are user-scoped, which no generic DOM read can answer, so claiming it anyway would be manufacturing findings. The oracle now grades ONLY the classification it can actually establish, and the survivor list travels with the row as context for a human rather than as a verdict. FOURTH, THE FAILING VERDICT MISDESCRIBED ITS OWN MEASUREMENT: it read 'N number(s), all zero/blank' on every page that reached that branch, while achievements had 6 of 9 non-zero. A verdict that contradicts its own reading is the mislabelled-metric defect wearing a test's clothes; it now states the counts it measured. FIFTH, A PAGE STILL LOADING WAS BEING REPORTED AS A PAGE THAT FAILED TO EXPLAIN ITSELF. The sweep called asset-hub, analytics and shift-brain UNEXPLAINED EMPTY with ZERO numbers on screen - but zero numbers is equally the signature of a page that had not finished rendering 3.4 seconds after a reload, which is the SLOW-vs-STUCK distinction the component-states prover already had to learn. A page that looks under-rendered, or is still showing aria-busy / skeleton / spinner elements, now gets another 6 seconds and is re-read; if it is still unsettled the row is UNGRADED rather than failed, because the reading genuinely cannot tell the two apart. SIXTH, THE ORACLE WAS FAILING PAGES THAT HAVE NO SUBJECT. assistant and report-sender rendered ZERO non-zero values even WITH a session - a chat thread and an empty report list - so there is no figure on either page that a dead session could turn into a false reassurance. Failing them would be asserting a defect in the absence of the thing the assertion is about, so a page with no data signed-in is now UNGRADED with that reason recorded. Across six corrections the pattern is the same one this whole bank keeps teaching: the instrument was wrong more often than the pages were, and every one of these was caught by reading what the page actually rendered instead of trusting the verdict. SEVENTH, THE READINESS GUARD ITSELF WAS TOO BLUNT AND DISQUALIFIED FINISHED PAGES. Counting elements matching skeleton/spinner/aria-busy selectors by SELECTOR ALONE flipped public-feed from a correct pass to UNGRADED on 1 busy element at 2473 rendered characters, and did the same to engineering-design (3 at 1851) and report-sender (2 at 1176) - because pages routinely leave a skeleton node in the DOM with display:none once the real content arrives. A hidden skeleton is a template, not a loading state, so only VISIBLE busy elements count. EIGHTH, A PASSING VERDICT NAMED A MECHANISM IT HAD NOT ESTABLISHED: an unchanged page with no figures was labelled 'public-surface-identical-signed-out' and PASSED, which called project-report - a hive report page - a public surface purely because it renders no numbers in either state. Every PASS must now rest on POSITIVE evidence (a redirect, a prompt that appeared, a sentence that appeared, a stated reason for being empty); an unchanged reading and a view with no figures at all are both UNGRADED, with the reason recorded, so they stay owed rather than being banked on a label nobody proved. WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: this is V1, the page as it loads, and it settles the CLIENT's behaviour when the stored session is gone. It does not test an EXPIRED-but-present token (a different path: the server refuses and the client must translate that refusal), nor a session that dies mid-action while a write is in flight. Those are separate oracles and stay owed rather than inheriting this reading. The walk is NON-WRITING - it reads, clears client-side storage in its own browser context, and reloads - so it cannot have touched the shared test database.
